reviewText: La Madeleine has certainly become a beloved spot of mine since first moving to Albuquerque a couple of years ago. It features good food, quaint atmosphere, and friendly staff. I might actually be so bold as to say that I have never had a bad experience while dining in at La Madeleine. Though I often get the mouth-watering Chicken Pesto Pasta; my most recent visit saw me indulge on the Croque Monsieur sandwich. As is the case for most things on the menu, it was delicious and filling. Not to mention that the complimentary bread table near the fountain machine is a big plus. The restaurant is also consistently clean, which is always reassuring. Pastries are well presented and the restaurant does well to include calorie content information for all items. La Madeleine doesn’t get much human traffic despite being located in the busy uptown area; which is a shame as it has a lot to offer. With that said, I always look forward to my next visit and hope that if in the vicinity; you’ll choose to give it a chance as well.

reviewText: La Madeleine charged me 38$ to gatekeep and gaslight me. It was one of the worst experiences, period. I've been to this location before years ago, and this time I saw they had this "Croffle" and I thought I'd give it a try. My partner had the American Breakfast, and we had two drinks. I was charged $38.05, which I didn't think much of at the time. The drink dispenser was out of syrup on both Starry and Bubly Lime, but you couldn't tell till you drank it. The melon in fruit salad my order came with had been cut too near the rind but you couldn't tell till you ate it. They used to have fresh bread out as an appetizer, but that was gone too, though the butter and jam were still out. Unpleasant so far, but a pleasant meal could cover a lot of failures. Then my order was delivered. It was a single Croffle, no powdered sugar, with a 2oz plastic cup of syrup, and a strawberry cut in half that was an unhealthy shade of overripe. I took it back to the counter to ask if this was the right order, and the manager confirmed it was. I asked where the other Croffle was, and the lady looked me in the eyes and said it was two. I looked at her, then at the round Belgian waffle iron behind the counter. "Where's the powdered sugar and preserves?" She said I could pump my own from the condiment bar. That's the gaslighting. When King Solomon has handed a baby, he didn't cut it in half and say, "There, it's two babies." But La Madeleine seems to think that's how it works. The gatekeeping came into play when the manager returned with my sugared Croffle. She'd walked past a tub if sliced bread in plastic baggies. I asked her how much for the bread, since my meal was half the size the menu said. She said the bread was free and passed me some. Apparently, I had not met their complimentary loaf standards until I complained. The strawberry jam came from a ketchup pump and was mostly corn syrup with the consistency of catsup. The bread was not fresh and had some of that school lunch plastic bag smell and a stale, waxy texture. I can't figure out how my order came to 38$ and I wasn't given a receipt to check. If I hadn't been so pissed off by the point I tired it, I might have actually enjoyed the Croffle because it was tasty.

reviewText: We were shopping at Perkins Rowe and wanted to stop by for an early dinner. We've eaten here many times before and this, by far, was the worst experience ever. The restaurant was not very crowded so easy to find a table for the 3 of us. My wife and son ordered and I was last. My son is a growing teenager and has a huge appetite. Even though he's a kid, he has a man-sized appetite! All he wanted was pasta and butter. Easy enough, right? When it was my turn to order, I told the employee taking orders I have a gluten allergy. He then proceeded to scream throughout the kitchen: GLUTEN ALLERGY! I turned around and saw people standing behind me. I thought: could he not be a bit more discrete? It is no one else's business. I ordered a salad and he proceeded to scream to the kitchen staff: GLUTEN ALLERGY! While I appreciated his attention, I thought there could be a better way of handling this. I walked to the register to pay and found a table. When my son's food arrived, it was a kid's size serving of pasta. I think we counted how many pieces of penne were in the bowl. After he cleaned the bowl, he filled up on sourdough bread. After we ate, we went to the dessert section. No one there. I counted 4 employees standing approximately 4 feet away from me, I made eye contact with at least 2 of them. And no one acknowledged my presence or offered to help. I could have easily interrupted but thought, no, I wanted to see how long it would take before someone stopped the conversation long enough to see what I needed. Six minutes! reviewText: I would like to say that, being from San Antonio, I have gone to LM locations quite often and been totally impressed. I took my friend to this location on a trip to Katy expecting a good time, and my friend and I left agreeing that it was the worst form of service we have ever experienced in our lives. First off, we went there in the evening ordering breakfast, something that is served all day. When explaining to the lady at the register what our orders were, she had to take the menu from us and look at it more clearly because she did not seem to know what we were ordering or have any real experience with the menu at all (my friend ordered an iced latte and a breakfast crepe, I ordered a yogurt parfait). Everything seemed very much like the whole staff had just started working at this location, and was falling apart at the seams. When my friend got her drink, they didn’t even bother to give her a straw. I had to go and get this for her. The man who we just saw sweeping And mopping with dirty water in the back was the one to give my friend her meal, something that immediately was a red flag for both of us. My meal did not come out for 30 minutes. During that time, I went to the bathroom, and instead of hearing any sort of music I just heard some sort of Rosetta Stone English to French translation segment over the speakers, some thing that was scary and left me feeling like I was in the twilight zone or something. After waiting much too long for my yogurt parfait, we summoned the guy who is sweeping over to our table, showed him the receipt, and explained that I was still waiting on my yogurt parfait. He apologized and left, returning with a parfait that was not what I ordered. Instead of being my seven dollar yogurt parfait, it was one of the tiny two dollar dessert parfaits that was displayed in a box in front of the cash register. By that point, my friend and I were stunned. I thought of going up and complaining, but didn’t think it be worth the effort. We left. My first thought was that the worker was deliberately trying to scam me out of 4-5 dollars, but then my friend and I came to the agreement that he just genuinely did not know the menu whatsoever. This happened on January 31, just a few days ago. My friend and I are able to laugh about it the best we can, but it’s still very surprising and concerning. Very disappointed.

reviewText: My how things have changed, not for the better. We've been eating at La Madeline for 20 years. My wife and I nearly always get the same thing regardless of which location we're at, the baked chicken and the bow tie pasta. Saturday we changed things up. We noticed they no longer sold the bow tie pasta - which was GREAT, so we chose items on their list of "New" entrees. My wife got Chicken Cordon Bleu Baked Pasta and I got the Ham and Swiss Crepe. We also got a "Gillette". I asked the server what it was and he said it's a hashbrown, to which I asked, so it's kind of like a hashbrown and he said, no, IT'S A HASHBROWN! We really love the place. I don't usually don't review a restaurant at less than a 3, if ever. Unless something very, very bad happened. Something very, very bad is happening to La Madeline. We were disappointed and sad. But let me first say this, service was fast, clean and the employees were polite and nice. I'll start with the Gillette. With tax and tip it's almost $4.00. Almost anywhere a hashbrown is half that price, but I wasn't so concerned about the price, I knew I was getting a hashbrown when I ordered it. I didn't expect it to be crunchy, as in almost chip a tooth crunchy on the outside, and almost creamy on the inside. Very weird, very awful That's not why they get the bad review though, maybe that's just the way French hash browns are supposed to be, I'm totally serious. The review is because of the entrees. My dish, in the photo, looked like it would be filling. When it arrived I realized it was served on a normal sized plate but the photo of the entree must've been taken on a plate just the next size larger than a saucer for a coffee cup because you could've quadrupled the order and it would have easily fit on my plate. Before I even had a bite I was disappointed with the small serving size but hoping that it would taste good. So much for wishful thinking. I was grateful that there was ONLY 2 small crepes because if there'd been 4 I wouldn't even have eaten the last 2. I don't know why I even ate 2., When I say they were bad, I don't mean spoiled bad, or cooked badly. I'm saying they were so salty it was ridiculous. The cheese did not have a good taste, the ham was about paper thin and allegedly there was chicken in there too, somewhere. I don't know if the cheese was the culprit, the ham or both. When I was leaving I spoke to an employee who will remain anonymous and mentioned the salt problem.. They said "everyone says the same thing. I personally think it's the ham so when I order it I tell the Chef no ham, use turkey". I would never order it again, ever, and we may never go back either. If the Gillette and crepe were the only problem I'd rate the meal as a 2, if I was generous. My wife's entree was very good sized, probably 15 times the volume of my entree. It was so big that I even remarked before we took a bite that we may have to share some of that because my meal is so small and we could take it home and get 3 more meals out of it. We ate about 20% of it and agreed, no doggy bad. It was awful with a capital A. If we'd taken it home it would have gone straight to the trash. Nothing spoiled, nothing cooked wrong, just way too salty and the cheese was not very good tasting cheese. The "diced ham" wasn't even diced, it was the same shredded paper thin salty ham that I had in my crepe. If we'd never been to La Madeline before and had this meal, I'm 100% positive we'd never, ever eat there again. The 2 entrees were really that awful. The current menu is a game changer. There is no way they do not know how bad those items are, they only need to try them. On top of that, when multiple employees remarked, when I politely expressed my concerns about those 2 entrees, "we know, I'm so sorry, everyone says the same thing". Such a shame, place isn't the same. Never eating there again.

reviewText: Unbelievable! For a week and a half we communicated back and forth with Felipé, a manager at this location who assured us we had a reserved room for 20 for an event on Sunday 1/21/18. Great! Everything is set. Over $1000 was spent on food and decorations, come they day of the event, we called in to ask how early we can set up and at this point we were talking to the GM, a new voice, since everything had been arranged and communicated with Felipe, she was confused to say the least. According to the G.M, this was against their policy. How on Earth do your employees not know the policy? How does Felipe the manager not know the policy? He himself provided the dollar amount for the 'plates and utensils' fee. It was a week and half's worth of back and forth with him. Confirming, checking, asking what could be brought and what couldn't. All invitations were made out to this location. What a great nightmare and inconvenience! Just a couple of hours until the event and with over $1000 worth of food and decorations we were left without a place to hold the event. Food gone to waste, event cancelled. Who will refund my food and decoration expense? What makes this worse some guest traveled over 5 hours to make it, just to be sent back home. The GM, decides thay her best approach was to test our 'logic', she kept saying "do you really think it's logical for a restaurant to allow such thing" That's why we called Genius! We weren't going to watlz in on Sunday at 4:30 P.M. out of thin air with guests and our own food. Of course not! All this was confirmed with Felipe (Manager) before hand. GM was very unapologetic and even threatened with a lawyer if we did not stop asking for an explanation or a solution to THEIR mistake. I would definitely give it less than 1 star if possible.

reviewText: I'm a big fan of this restaurant chain, I was going to la Madeleine when it was still on Cherry Street, I decided to take my mom for lunch one day after we got done at a hike at Turkey mountain, the food was refreshing and delicious as always, the girl who took our order was nice I honestly don't remember her name I don't think anyone was wearing name tags and no one ever told me their name, the girl who was preparing the stuff at the hot bar like soup and other hot and ready items was curt and seems like she wanted to be anywhere else but there heavy on the attitude and eye rolling... I stood there at the soup counter staring at my tomato bisque, already prepared and sitting in a ramekin waiting for my sandwich so I didn't ask for my soup even though I saw it there, a woman behind me who looked like she might have been a manager or something was in a meeting with an older gentleman and asked me if there was anything I needed, I politely told her that I was still waiting on my soup and sandwich, she went back to her conversation and I stood there for another 5 minutes and then she prompted me again and asked me what I was standing there waiting on and I reminded her my soup and sandwich and she asked the girl who was heavy on the attitude to give me my soup and then told me my sandwich would be a few more minutes, I was confused because normally the half sandwich and soup are serve together, as for me personally I really like dipping my sandwich in my soup so I couldn't eat the two separately, and by the time my sandwich had been delivered my soup was lukewarm/ room temp... It wasn't my most favorite experience with la Madeleine but I know them to be an exceptional company with exceptional food so I'm just counting this as a one-off. As for the atmosphere in my opinion the location on Cherry Street had the atmosphere nailed, and the service of an all day French cafe, but as we all have to sever now without that location, the one in Tulsa hills is the only one we have access to, and I feel like they still have a lot of work to do on the atmosphere and the vibe that the people who work their give off.

reviewText: This is I think my favorite La Madeleine of all the ones I’ve been to. Here I find friendly and very hardworking people. Lorena brings out our meals with a smile. And she takes good care of the dining room, along with Rosita. The managers are friendly and they help out to make sure everything is working smoothly and everyone is taken care of. I always enjoy the meals and they are priced affordably. There are so many options in the menu to try so food is never boring. Add to that the fact that they change it up a bit to offer special seasonal meals that are delicious. They offer a Cafe Sampler where you get to choose a combination of 3 items (salad, soup, fruits, etc.). They also have amazing salads and sandwiches that you can order whole or in combination with a side of your choice. They have a huge dining area, including an outside seating. Beverage & bread counters are in the dining area so you can freely serve yourself and go for seconds, if you wish. And they’re great at serving fresh coffee. The bakery offers tempting desserts. Make sure to get their La Madeleine app and sign up for their rewards - that way you make every visit count towards free items or special offers.

reviewText: La Madeleine was a fantastic spot to kick off a day in Irving, as I took my friend who had visited from another part of the world. Each bite was a true delight, particularly the muffins and croissants. And, of course, no breakfast would be complete without a steaming cup of coffee. It was delightful to see numerous morning joggers enjoying their coffee, muffins, and croissants. I wholeheartedly recommend La Madeleine to anyone seeking a scrumptious and laid-back breakfast to begin their day perfectly in Irving.

reviewText: We had a pretty bad experience there today. We ordered our food and were told it would be around 15 minutes. 35 minutes later we got a third of our order. We finally get our soups 10 minutes later and they were cold, as was my husband's au jux. Add 10 more minutes and my mom hadn't gotten her main dish yet. Waiter came around to say it would be another 5 minutes until it was ready. My mom waited almost an hour when she had been told her food would be ready in 12 to 14 minutes. It was all together really bad service but I'll give it 3 stars because the manager was very sorry and gave us $30 in gift cards to apologize. I've been to other La Madeleines before and had never experience bad service. I'll give this one the benefit of the doubt and try again another time. Hopefully they just had a rough evening or were maybe understaffed, so we'll see. I'll update my review the next time I come.

reviewText: We are regular customers at this Location on Sam Houston Parkway around the Memorial Area. This restaurant chain is unfortunately on the downfall. Here are the reasons why. They no longer put the chicken in the foil wrap, the chicken that is used for the chicken Caesar salad was cold, and not warm/hot like they used to do it when they wrapped it around in tin foil and had it in the warmer section. The Dressing portion that they provided with the salad was half-filled, how in the world is that enough dressing for the whole chicken Caesar salad? They are being selfish on the salad dressing, so its pretty much obvious they are trying to cut down costs, but these cut downs impact the user experience. Third, The Chicken Friand was really dry, even with the mushroom sauce added on. The Chicken Friand itself is super dry and the chicken isn't as tender and soft as it usually is. I have been a customer at La Madeline since I was in my high school years, I am 38 and now and this will be my first negative review for the restaurant. reviewText: My wife and I went to La Madeleine for breakfast because we had been given a gift card. I ordered an omelette and asked if they had gluten free bread option and they said no. I then asked if I could substitute something like fruit for the croissant and they said no. If you go to Denny's they have both gluten free muffins (which are very nice) and they will substitute fruit in place of bread. My wife also asked for a substitute in her order and they said no. Apparently there are no substitutions at all! When we went to pay we were told their gift card reader was not working. There was no sign out saying that the card reader was not working. You think the manager might have apologized and offered some sort of compensation, but La Madeleine does not do anything like this apparently. The food was OK but nothing special. For the same money you can have a lot better omelette at Denny's or IHOP, with much better service. There are admittedly some distinct lunch/dinner options like the caesar salad and the tomato basil soup which are worth going to La Madeleine for. My wife and I really like the ambiance at La Madeleine, like we always have. But the food is not all that special and the service stinks. We will use up our gift cards (assuming they get their card reader working) but we probably won't go back after that. Or if we do it definitely won't be for breakfast.

reviewText: Many years ago la Madeleine would have received five stars. I went for breakfast two or three days a week, and frequently went for lunch. The food was great, the ambiance was great, and the service was good. Unfortunately over the years it became corporatized and much of the food appears to be prepared off premises and only heated on premises. It was the most convenient place to go to lunch, so we decided to try it again. A mistake. There is no longer easily available free bread and butter, even with soup. My French dip had barely any meat, and the meat was dry. Overall, I just recommend avoiding it.

reviewText: From the moment you step into this warm and inviting cafe, you're transported to a quaint French bistro that's both cozy and elegant. The tomato basil soup is a must-try, with its rich, velvety texture and perfectly balanced flavors. While the Caesar salad was just okay, it's still a refreshing and light complement to any meal. Moving on to the entrees, the creamy pesto pasta with shrimp is a standout dish that's both creamy and flavorful, with perfectly cooked shrimp adding a touch of sweetness to the dish. The chicken la Madeleine is another highlight, cooked to perfection and served with a delectable side of creamy mashed potatoes. And let's not forget about dessert! The creme brulee is an indulgent treat that's both creamy and satisfying, with the perfect amount of caramelized sugar on top. And of course, no trip to La Madeleine is complete without trying their signature Madeline cookies, which are the perfect sweet ending to any meal. Overall, La Madeleine in Mockingbird, Dallas is a must-visit destination for those seeking a taste of France in the heart of Texas. I would definitely return to this location. reviewText: I am a very frequent customer of this restaurant for a pretty good while for about a year. I always order through Uber eats to save time and I have always enjoyed their food especially the sandwiches. However recently starting about a month ago, they decided to switch the bread of the sandwiches to a much smaller size. Mind you that they have always had decent proportions in terms of the bread size since you can choose half or whole in size when you are ordering the sandwich. It always was about a good 9 to 10 inch sandwich for the whole portion to which you can even save the other half for later. Now it is literally just a 6 inch sub cut in half with another type of bread. Absolutely ridiculous. I’m not sure what made them to do this decision, whether it’s for financial reasons but it’s a poor excuse knowing that this is a chain restaurant throughout the United States. I’m not sure if it’s other restaurants also doing the same thing so I’m going to test out the one up in Dallas when I go there this weekend for the Fourth of July to see if they are doing the same thing. Or if it’s just the location of the Huebner Oaks shopping Center. Big disappointment! Especially being that the restaurant is close to me and other business areas nearby.

reviewText: As much as I would like to give this place 5 stars I rather share in hopes of management improving to keep La Madeleine as a well loved restaurant with great service, atmosphere and food. With that being said the restrooms are poorly kept. They smell very bad and always smell the same. They look old and floors are sticky and dirty. The staff is nice, not too talkative, but they will chat and be kind when spoken to. The fireplace on when the weather is cooler or maybe for the evening time to set a nice ambiance would be wonderful, but once nowhen I asked to turn it on the manager said it is not cold outside, so they won't be turning it on. I think the location on champion forest is much better, except I live closer to this one. I can only hope new things are in-store for this location on 290 frwy and 1960. Update to my last review: Today is Oct 30, 2018 I can't say it was my review that made a difference, but all that matters is that La Madeleine at the NW frwy did make great changes to the restroom issue. Today I walked in the ladies room, no sticky mopped floor, no bad smell, I think they added this furniture piece as well and hung a few frames on the wall. It looks better and smells better, makes me happy to see this and that maybe "my review " made a difference. Thanks La Madeleine!! *Also, a few weeks ago we came in on a cooler morning and asked to have the fireplace turned on and thankfully the manager took care of that! :-)

reviewText: I ate here on 3/28/21 at the location in Webster TX. Essentially what you are getting is the "French" version of Jason's Deli (not that there is anything wrong with that). Upon getting our food and eating our food, the manager comes to our table, She stated that she had to wring up the order again as it "didn't go through". We showed her our receipt but she still insisted upon ringing it up again. How did it not "go through" if we had a receipt showing the order had gone through? Essentially, we were charged twice for the same meal. I asked her what the plan was since we shouldn't have to pay for the same food twice. I was told the double charge "would be removed at the end of the day". That isn't a solution and said so. The manager told me that she had a new cashier and he had made the same mistake on three tables. That isn't my problem. I shouldn't have to pay twice due to their inability to train their staff. The manager gave a half hearted "apology" and then turned on the tears as a sympathy ploy but offered no other solution. Bottom line: If you like small portions, poorly trained staff, and management that has no clue how to handle employee mistakes, La Madeleine is the restaurant for you.

It tasted stale and old,   I could not taste or smell any butter. And for the price of  $5.69 for 2, I could have gotten a dozen croissants from Costco that taste better. So disappointed, the quality of the food is not the same any more.

UPDATE

09/05/21 After the owners reached out to me and offer a complimentary Bon Apatite card. I went back and got the same 2 croissants and a fruit tart. I am sorry to say I cannot  raise my star rating although customer service was good. The croissants looks really nice and glossy outside, but inside it is dry and crumbly and taste stale. It is almost like the recipe or ingredients are change. It does not taste like the other store. reviewText: La Madeleine has been one of my favorite lunch spots since I was a teenager. I used to visit with friends and my mom and now I take my adult daughter. I like how it is consistent no matter which restaurant I visit in any city. That was not the case with our first visit to the Forum location. The restaurant was not well kept, the whole place smelled like dirty dish rags and most tables were covered with crumbs and sticky stuff. The food was awful. I ordered the Chicken Friand with a Caesar salad and it was room temperature. It tasted like it had been sitting out for a couple of days and the mushroom sauce was cold. The salad was a soggy plate of greens and soggy croutons. It was as if it had been tossed in the dressing hours before but you couldn't taste it the dressing.. My daughter ordered the chicken Madeleine and it was NASTY. The rice was weird and tasted metallic. The chicken was bland and bone dry and the broccoli was unseasoned mush. The only redeeming items were the the Turkey Bistro sandwich and tomato soup. They were tasty as always. It is frustrating when you spend almost $50 on lunch and it is inedible. I waited in line for 5 minutes to try and speak to the manager but I was never acknowledged. We left our full plates behind and went home and ate. I honestly would have a better meal rooting around in the dumpster behind Panera.

reviewText: I came to this restaurant when it first opened in 2017, and had a bad experience with not being acknowledged after standing at the counter for quite some time and I never even got a chance to try any of the food. I searched for gluten free desserts in Albuquerque on Monday for my daughter’s Birthday, and decided to give it another shot. When I walked in, I could see a young man and a young woman standing in front of the back wall in front of the kitchen window, and a chef in the kitchen. I walked up to the counter in front of the desserts and all three of the employees looked at me, but then looked away and continued with their conversation. I stayed in front of the glass and then looked around the area there at the front to see if there was a sign or something that showed where I should go for help since the employee weren’t coming to me. Finally after a couple of minutes the girl came over to the counter and asked if I needed help.I told her that I was wanting to know which deserts were gluten free. She said she had “no idea” and then just stood there. I said that the search had lead me there so that was why I was asking. She didn’t say anything again and I just looked at her and she said “I guess I can ask”. I was already frustrated and said “uh, that would be helpful” she walked away and came back to say they didn’t have anything gluten free. I then walked out the door. I was NOT upset about no gluten free options, I was upset about receiving such bad service again two years later. It takes a lot for me to give a bad review, but this one was worth the one star I gave it. I was hoping for better service and to actually get to try the food. I guess I never will because I won’t be coming back. Great service is key in any successful business.

reviewText: Our experience was extremely disappointing. On the morning of 10/5, we decided to have a breakfast date before my wife headed to work. We ultimately requested a refund. This required staff to call the associate manager from the back to handle it. When the manager finally came out, there was no apology, no acknowledgment of our experience—just a refund, and that was it. What bothered me most wasn’t just the long wait or the missing items—it was the complete disregard from the associate manager, who stayed hidden in the back while her team struggled up front. If they were truly short-staffed, why wasn’t she helping? Between the lack of customer service, poor communication, and the dirty, poorly maintained environment, we left completely disgusted. No guest should have to deal with this. Period. Update: I contacted la madeleine customer service. A franchise business consultant reached out to apologize and mentioned training would happen for employees. Nothing was offered other than a thank you and appreciation for letting them know of the issues. This is truly when I believed they lost touch with customer service. reviewText: I am a long-time fan of La Madeleine. This restaurant has deliciously prepared food. Also, they play classical music. In an age when so many restaurants, waiting rooms, etc. have TVs blaring, THANK GOODNESS someone still values music with a meal. Now to the food...My very favorite thing is the Tomato Basil Soup. I love the tomatoey rich flavor. Next favorite is a Croque Monseiur, a sandwich made with ham and a topping of rich bechamel and cheese and broiled. Half of one is perfect for breakfast! The coffee is always delicious and they have plenty of real half-and-half. A very attractive feature of this restaurant is the bread bar, which includes a selection of breads, real butter and homemade jams and honey. Another thing worth mentioning...the roast chicken. If you go at lunch, the wonderful smell permeates the whole place. Roast chicken and Caesar Salad are perfect together. Oh, and the icing on the cake is their pastries!! I cannot choose a favorite one, but the fruit tart, the Sacher torte and the almond croissant are wonderful. And the lemon tart. And the strawberries Romanoff are also just delicious. I love everything I have ever eaten here. It really is wonderful.

reviewText: I'm not too certain people on Google reviews know how to honestly rate an establishment without sounding like a bunch of whiners. reviewText: La Madeline has been my go-to for decades anytime I traveled to TX. The chain never disappoints & the French Country Breakfast is my usual. Until this time… First, we and several folks behind us waited at the register for over 10 minutes while staff flittered around us without saying one word to acknowledge that we were there. A woman in a beanie finally strolled; dragging her feet from the back. Took our order and we sat down. After 8 minutes, we decided to ask about our mimosa’s where we were told they didn’t know. Ok, weird as it was rang up in the POS but not a biggie, it happens sometimes. Few minutes later, they brought out the OJ, glasses & champagne for us to make ourselves. Keep in mind, it took 10 minutes to order, 8 min for our kit to make mimosas and then another 14 for our breakfast. I kept looking at my plate trying to figure out what was missing. Once I realized the part that made it “French” potato galette was missing, I went up to ask. She quickly brushed me off and said I have them in the oven. I decided to put a timer on it bc by now I’m just irritated— who wants to eat a dry hash brown alone? It took 21 minutes & 24 seconds for it to come out ALMOST COOKED. We almost gave up on it because our meal was eaten so far in advance. Lastly, while I was waiting, I went to refill my coffee only to find out the coffee was totally removed from its location. Listen, I understand businesses are dealing with finding good help resulting in running lean. But from what I could see, I counted 5 staff members minus the cooks in the back. With this store being a much smaller restaurant (& the restaurant only being half full) in comparison to most, I don’t understand the inconsistency this store represented today. Sigh, bummed 😑

reviewText: Soon to be a casualty -- Reply to owner...going to the La Madeleine website won't solve the real problem with your restaurant. If you are the manager, I suggest you take better care of the place. Clean it! Improve the quality of the food! It's not a corporate issue. It's a local manager issue! We went to the La Madeleine in Downtown Crown for dinner this week and will not be back. The place was dirty - tables had not been cleared or wiped down, the bathroom hadn't been cleaned for quite some time. The food was mediocre at best. I order the Croque Monsieur and French onion soup. Neither were hot, the sandwich only had a few slices of meat and no cheese; the soup was extremely thick and didn't taste good at all. Soda fountain Pepsi was flat. My husband ordered the tomato soup which was very thick and cold. His French dip was bready and barely had any meat or cheese on it. This place used to be reliably good, but the past few times it has been disappointing. I could understand the dirty tables if they didn't have staff available, but the employees were standing clustered around the register talking with little regard for the condition of the place. Trust me, it's not worth the money spent to eat here.

reviewText: Potato soup tastes instant, grainy, watery. No fresh potatoes are used in this dish. reviewText: My wife introduced me to this french style restaurant over a decade ago and I have been a customer ever since. I have only had there lunch/dinner items never been in for breakfast unfortunately. They have great fresh food. I enjoy quite a variety of items of their menu which considering how picky I am with food says a lot. I love their chicken cesar salad their croutons dressing and chicken always get top ratings from me. I also love their chicken Parisian sandwich as well as the chicken salad croissant. They used to have bowtie pasta salad that was really good but they changed to penne pasta and it has not hit the mark at least in me and my wife's opinion. They also have great soups. Their tomato basil is good enough it is jarred and sold in the restaurants and grocery stores, I also get the country potato with cheese and bacon sure does make you feel great. Lastly their baked goods I would have to say we like nearly all of their desserts. They do awesome breads and a delicious strawberry rhubarb jam that pairs perfectly.

Not only did he correct my order, he doubled my dessert (the lemon tarts are amazing!) AND he gave me a $10 gift card to use during my next visit. That is what I call outstanding customer service! reviewText: Expectations have to be managed when walking into a la Madeleine, but in general this is one of the better locations. There's a nice fireplace in the dining area and it's reasonably big in comparison to the one in the River Oaks area (for example). If you're not familiar, you order at a counter, pay, and bring back a marker - then they bring your food out to you. They have complimentary jam and bread; neither is anything great the bread is hard and the jam is prepackaged. Drinks are also self-serve and includes tea, soda and water. There's also wine but that you have to order. As part of my search for good food with calorie counts listed, I came here several times in a row trying different combinations of soups and sandwiches. Here are the sad results: the soup is best. Tomato basil: ridiculously salty. I can't believe they sell jars of these; do people water them down when they get home? Country Potato: actually pretty nice; but be careful if you're calorie counting they will add cheese and bacon etc. to the top; ask for the soup without the toppings if you want to save on calories. Otherwise it's a nice filling, thick soup. Jambon-Buerre: I tried the ham and the swiss separately to figure out which of them was providing that almost chemical taste to my sandwich. I concluded that it was both. I'm scared to try the croque-monsieur because I assume it's made with the exact same ham and swiss. There was an exorbitant amount of butter on this. The baguette is actually really lovely. You might consider just getting a baguette. Chicken Salade Croissant: Oh so sad. The croissant isn't buttery or flaky at all; rather something waxy like the ones they have a Walmart. The chicken salad is also pretty sad; flavorless and drenched in mayo to mask the lack of quality of the chicken. French Dip: Horrendous roast beef quality. The best thing about this sandwich was also the baguette. The stale taste of the poor quality roast beef is doubled by the fact that it is served hot. They accept contactless payment.

reviewText: Definitely one of the better managed La Madeleine bistros. Light crowd on a cold day was not the reason for the delightful experience. The staff were professional and friendly but not invasive. Good day for the signature dishes plus the popular pastries. Sadly, we saw several parfait items on the way but since we wanted to these to-go, we thought it best to order these on the way out. Naturally, Mr. Murphy paid a visit while we were dining and much to our dismay all the chocolate parfait had been sold and there was none for us to-go. Lesson learnt - grab as quickly as you can. Obviously there were many other excellent pastries for us to compensate for our mistake. Good solid experience here means it will become a regular pit stop for us. It is as French as faux Cajun is for those who haven't tasted the real stuff but we don't mind it at all (having had the genuine stuff in France). The same could be said for any other international cuisine. So we ignore country designator and simply enjoy La Madeleine food as it is offered.

reviewText: I never, ever write negative reviews. It's just not something I do. I love writing positive reviews, but this time I cannot hold back. I feel so nostalgic about La Madeleine. I remember a time with the food was incredible. Fresh, beautiful, wholesome. But they have clearly sold their soul and cut every possible corner but kept prices high. My business partner and I had breakfast for $45 for two French Country Breakfasts, French toast and two cups of tea. The eggs were ordered over-medium and came out looking like shoe leather all tough and brown. They were entirely inedible. I was raving about the potato galette but ours had sat on the warming plate so long (this is still only 9 am) and were tough and chewy. La Madeleine used to have the most marvelous strawberry and blackberry jams - made with real fruit. Now you get served a plastic thimble filled with a liquidy sugar that has some strawberry or blackberry juice. Overly sweet with no taste of the fruit. They used to have rotisserie chickens but corporate gutted the soul of freshness and realness and now they use factory-made, frozen chicken in the salads. I used to love the lemon tarts - but now for $4+ dollars they give you the tiniest of tarts that is mostly sugar cookie shell. Just not worth it. It's the classic sweetened condensed milk + egg+ lemon tart. I can make a whole pie of that for less. It is just so sad to see this once shining star of the "fast casual" dining experiences just go down the drain. I never minded paying their premium for the food because it used to be good. We seriously would have gotten better hash browns at Ihop or McDonald's. Just don't disappoint yourself and unload your wallet at the same time. You don't need to add insult to injury.

reviewText: I dined at your restaurant this afternoon. I won't go into detail about how delicious the food was—though it certainly was—but what I really want to share is something that happened afterward. After finishing my meal, I left in a bit of a rush and accidentally forgot to take my backpack with me. Inside the backpack were my passport and wallet, so when I realized I had left it behind, I was extremely anxious, fearing it might have been taken by someone else. By the time I returned to the restaurant, it had already been two hours since I left. When I asked the staff if anyone had seen my backpack, a young waitress told me that she had found it and had tried to find a way to contact me. Unfortunately, there was no contact information inside, so she decided to keep it safe for me in the meantime. She then kindly returned the backpack to me. I’m incredibly grateful to your restaurant and to that young waitress (I was so relieved and overjoyed to have my bag back that I forgot to ask her name). I would like to express my appreciation for the honesty and kindness shown by your staff.

reviewText: 💕There’s a couple of things that I loved about this place: 1. Customers order at the register instead of the table. 2. You immediately get your dessert or paisley from the bakery as soon as you pay for it. In essence, the baked goods are like appetizers but much FASTER. 3. The kind staff greets you when you come in and when you leave 💚🤍💚🤍 4. The tables and restrooms were clean. Note: The bathroom decals are in French. Just an FYI, Madame means ‘Mrs’ so that you walk into the right restroom. 5. The food was delicious and my entire order was under $38! I ordered a build your own omelette which is originally under $12 with three ingredients. I had tomatoes, spinach, onions, bacon, and cheese. Yes , I know you can order and one te anywhere but this is what I had a taste for 🍳🥚🧀🥓🍅🥬🧅The omelet comes with two slices of tomatoes so you don’t have to add it to the omelet if you wish to save money. Since each ingredient is $1 more , I paid $14, not bad. My daughter ordered a kid’s scrambled egg and bacon with a side of fruit. The kid’s meals are under $6. Each of our meals came with a croissant. In additions, I ordered to vanilla fruit parfaits that were each under $3 and a great proportion. I am very picky about parfaits but the baker did very well with the taste and size ! The fruit didn’t taste watery like some other places. Also, the fruit salad watermelon was cut the perfect bit size. It was sweet and fresh ! If I sound picky, I might be 🤓 6. The atmosphere is very relaxed/ laidback and I saw many different groups of people just as if you were really in 🇫🇷💙 When you walk in, it seems like all the elderly people sit to the right and anyone under 40 seemed to take a left. 7. The baristas/waitresses were wearing cute berets because that’s…. Classic French👌🏽 8. The drinks are self serve. Additional comments: Kind staff and clean bathrooms matter ! ✅💚 This is a snob free environment. There was a rude customer who received judgy eyes for her behavior to kindly let her know to behave 🌝 The croissant was a little dry but still good. I ordered French coffee but the French coffee dispenser was empty. I ended up drinking American which was not any change in price. Four stars total for the great experience and my daughter wants to come back to this family / kid friendly cafe 😊⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

reviewText: ⭐⭐⭐ We had our breakfast at la Madeleine, and overall it was a pleasant experience with a few ups and downs. The ordering system is quick and convenient, which makes things easy — but in trying to be fast, some of the quality gets lost. The coffee wasn’t very flavorful, and the hygiene of some serving areas could definitely be improved. That said, the food itself was really good, and the pastries were amazing — probably the best part of the whole experience. The decor also stands out. It feels like you’ve stepped into a cozy countryside house — with brick walls, exposed pipes, and a warm, rustic charm. I really loved the atmosphere. I’ve been to this place multiple times, sometimes for just coffee and other times for meals. It’s always busy and full of people, which shows how popular it is. The staff are friendly and always smiling, which adds to the positive vibe. For me, I wish the quality of coffee and cleanliness matched the great decor and delicious pastries. Still, it’s an acceptable experience overall, especially if you love cozy places with a good pastry selection.

reviewText: Me encantó la experiencia en esta cafetería (Webster, Texas) por las siguientes razones: ambientación, carta, atención y calidad de los productos. Su oferta de pastelería se inspira en las tradiciones francesas, entre las que destaco variedades locales de pie de limón, tartaleta de frutas y pastel de chocolate. Además de sándwiches, también hay bebestibles y productos envasados como mermeladas. Se puede consumir en la misma cafetería o pedir para llevar. Mención aparte merece el sector de los baños, donde, mientras uno se encuentra haciendo uso de ellos, se escucha una voz femenina en off que da clases de francés (con traducciones al inglés, obviamente), en un acento muy castizo y que convierte a esta experiencia en algo más académico y divertido de lo que pudiera ser en cualquier otra parte. Recomendable ciento por ciento.

My visit here today has been of the upmost pleasure. I have standards set very high in regards to French Cuisine.

Truly my visit today has given me a very sweet reminder of Albi France and the culture therein. Thank you for a fantastic meal and wonderful environment.

Les chefs qui ont préparé mes repas ont à la fois satisfait et dépassé mes attentes concernant les repas que j'ai commandés. Le goût était excellent. Les saveurs de la viande et des légumes se marient parfaitement.

J'ai vraiment adoré les déserts. Fabriqué à la perfection et à l'excellence.
Vraiment ma visite d'aujourd'hui m'a donné un très doux rappel d'Albi France et de la culture qui s'y trouve. Merci pour un repas fantastique et un environnement merveilleux

reviewText: Their bakery selections are absolutely scrumptious. You can taste the freshness and quality ingredients in every bite. Just looking at them makes your mouth water in anticipation. They had a fresh french bread bar across from the drink station that had butter and two kinds of jam to go along with the two kinds of french bread. reviewText: La Medline is an absolute gem for anyone who appreciates high-quality European-style cuisine. Their eggs Benedict, served on a perfectly toasted baguette with a velvety hollandaise sauce, is pure perfection. reviewText: My experience at La Madeleine was incredibly disappointing. My mother had been eager to visit this place during our vacation in Pasadena after hearing about it from a friend. Despite several family members warning us that the restaurant wasn’t great, we decided to give it a try to make my mom happy. At first glance, the restaurant seemed cozy and inviting, but unfortunately, the service left much to be desired. It was, without a doubt, the worst customer service we experienced during our two weeks in Houston. From the moment we walked in, there was zero empathy or willingness to guide us through the process. The menu was outdated and worn, and we were confused about how to order since they offered à la carte options, a buffet, and a bakery. When we asked for help, the instructions were vague at best. When it came time to place our order, we were directed to another staff member who was incredibly rude. She handled our payment, and we asked where we would get our coffee—whether we should wait for it there or if it would be brought to our table. Her response was dismissive, repeating over and over that the coffee "would come to us." I asked again for clarification, and she snapped back with an irritated tone, saying the same thing. Once we sat down with our food, the coffee never arrived. When we asked the person serving the food about it, she said we needed to serve ourselves. The same rude cashier returned and curtly told us that black coffee is self-serve, as though we should have known that. I tried to explain that this was exactly what I had been asking earlier, but she became defensive and acted as if it was my fault for not understanding their process. How could I possibly know how things work in a place I’ve never been before? I came here to give my mother a pleasant experience, not to deal with staff who lacked basic courtesy. The food was mediocre, the place may have been cozy, but the atrocious customer service completely overshadowed everything. I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone. Save your time and money and go somewhere else.

reviewText: I've always enjoyed my visits to La Madeleine, but this particular one is what made me sit down and write a review. I received news today that a family member passed, so I was a little depressed walking in. I was looking forward to the lemon madeleines, my favorite bakery item there, but they were out. I was understandably bummed out. Well, we get our food and sit down to eat. My husband discovers his eyes were too big for his stomach, and he doesn't have the room to finish his coffee drink. I walked up to the cashier and asked for a to-go cup and expected that to be the end of it. Instead, she offered to pour it into the cup for us, and she warmed it up for him without us asking. Then, as we're standing up to leave, the same gentleman I asked about the lemon madeleines caught me as we were about to walk out and handed me a small plate with a single madeleine on it, fresh from the oven. He said he saw how disappointed I looked when he told me they were out, and had a fresh one brought to me. Those two small gestures really turned my day around. I was really down after getting the news of the death in the family, but their wonderful customer service and their going above and beyond brought a smile to my face. Linda and Ricky were their names, and that restaurant is fortunate to have such great staff that genuinely care about customer service. Thank you both for helping to make my sad day just a little happier. You have a lifelong patron.

reviewText: Simply can't go wrong with anything from La Madeleine. Simple French classic food. It was my sister's prom night so of course she is still watching her weight so she wanted a salad. We ordered the salade sampler which you can choose from a list of items that are all tasty. Since she wanted salads, I decided to order her all three of their salads: Caesar, Bacon Strawberry and Cranberry Walnut. All three salads were dressed nicely and each bite was delicious. And for myself, I ordered the Country Potato Soup, which is to die for! Honestly one of my favorite soups ever! If I was ever sick or having a bad day, this soup cures all blues! They top it off with bacon and cheddar cheese and OMG salty bacon and creamy cheese you simply can't go wrong! After all this food, it was a must that I got a dessert so I ordered the Strawberry Napoleon and you can say I was a happy camper! Each layer of the puff pasty was cooked perfectly mixed the bavarian cream! SO GOOD!

reviewText: To the employee with blue hair and bad service. I love La Madeleine. I have been coming to this location for the past 10 years and have always had a wonderful experience with both the food and service. Two nights ago, my boyfriend and I had ordered, had our meal inside, and were about to leave when we decided to stop by the bakery to grab a dessert on our way out. Waiting in line a few minutes to closing behind a customer who was ordering. By the time they finished and received their order, the time was apparently 3 minutes after closing and the person at the front, a lady with blue hair, said "Oh we're closed now." To which we responded in confusion. She then further proceeded to repeat herself saying, "Yeah we closed at 9" and it was 3 minutes after closing and we hadn't realized. We explained to her that we were already waiting behind the customer before us before they were closed and while it didn't seem like she was gonna serve us, someone else said to her, just serve them. She proceeded to roll her eyes and take our order. We were out of there in 3 minutes. You never, never talk to a customer that way. I get people walking in right as you close or even after closing because they see people are still inside, I get the frustration of that, but no matter when they walk in, you serve them. That's customer service. You never let them stand in line and when the clock hits closing, try to turn them away. Terrible service and someone ought to tell this girl otherwise.

reviewText: I have always loved this chain, and had a good mark at this location a few years ago, but, my, how they have fallen down! The young gal who took our order at the register clearly didn’t want to be there — and made us feel like she didn’t want us there. Normally, La Madeleine, in keeping with its French tradition, has fresh breads, jams, and butter out. Here they just had a few leftovers out from the previous day, though they had been open almost an hour, plus no jam or butter. So I asked. I did get a helpful, apologetic man to bring out jam and butter. He noticed the few pieces of bread and said, “Oh, they didn’t bring the bread out? Let me get it!” So, I thought, “All’s well that ends well. At least I will be getting fresh bread now.” Au contraire, mes frères ! He brought out a tray from the fridge under a cellophane wrap, upon which a sticker indicated the bread had been baked the previous day and was to be tossed the next. To top it off, he didn’t take the cellophane off! But that’s not the “best” part: this day-old cellophane wrapped bread was placed in front of a huge poster on the wall that featured a bread chef and pictures of bread with the caption, “Baked here at 5am daily”! My potato galette was clearly reheated. Probably microwaved. Wife’s french toast OK, but her sausage was rubbery. Probably nuked also. I don’t mind La Mad’s prices when you get what you come in for. reviewText: The first time I ate here, with shortly after they opened the restaurant. It was so busy that they couldn't keep up, brought us the wrong food, brought us food that was cooked the wrong way, in a general just botched the whole meal. So, I waited half a year to come back and try it again. Six months later... The food is okay. The folks seem very nice. This time, it wasn't crowded at all. The food was cooked correctly, but they didn't really have what I wanted. Specifically, I prefer my eggs poached, and they either don't know how to do that, or have some sort of Health code issue with cooking them that way. I will say that the first time I was here they did have poached eggs. Of course, they didn't cook them right and I complained about it. So maybe, they just took them off the menu. All in all, the food was okay. The French toast was very crispy and delicious. Parisian eggs were just okay. That said, I everything on my plate, so it can't have been that bad. 12 Months later... All in all, this is an okay place to go. I end up not going to get very often because they don't poach eggs. That's kind of my favorite way to have headaches so, I take that into consideration when I consider going here. Let's forget about the eggs for a while. Here are other good things about this place. The Ambiance is nice. I really like the decor. And, I like other menu items. They have a fried potato side dish that's really very good. They have quiche, which is tricky to pull off. And they have an array of baked items that are just delicious. As I pointed out to someone in answer to their question about the restaurant, they have a pretty good coffee bar. It's self serve, so you fix it the way you like. I think they have a bottomless cup concept here, so you get as much as you want. They also have a fresh baked bread section that's self-serve. On that station are jellies, jams, and butter. That's pretty good too. I enjoy going back to get a variety of combinations of Breads and jams.

reviewText: Not terrible, but we weren't impressed. It felt like we were in line at a Furr's cafeteria, and the food was about the same quality. Everyone stands in a line, often stretching onto the sidewalk, and menus are passed out. Customers are told to choose what they want before they get up to the counter, to ensure that the line moves quickly. A server takes orders towards the front, as customers stand in line, and instructs everyone to keep following the line. Felt like a cattle chute--but it was lunch rush. Servers behind a glass pane hand out soups and sandwiches along the line, if customers ordered them, and you pay and collect your drinks and a number for your table at the end. Like I said, think Furr's/Flying Star. We should have read more about the place before going in--we didn't expect that type of dining environment, and I think that kind of threw everyone in my party off. The menu tempted us with tasty-looking mimosas, but alas--the place doesn't have its liquor license yet. Food was too salty for my taste. Pastries weren't anything special. The tomato basil soup was good! Tart. All in all not my cup of tea, but it is a very popular place, so obviously many other people enjoy it! Give it a try!

reviewText: My mom ate at La Madeleine from Maryland long time ago and I learned the other day that there's one in Louisiana and we decided to eat there for Lunch. When we got there, the parking space outside didn't feel right for us because we have to be aware of our surroundings and whatnot and it was very tight and not enough space. That aside, the inside of the restaurant was really nice and bright. It captures the essence of France very well and I like it. The desserts look really yummy and sinfully sweet. The dessert I ate was the "Fruit Tart" or something like that and I really enjoyed it very much because when it comes to eating foods like this, I prefer to take very little bites and savor the moment. My lunch tasted really good, as well. I think it was "Roast Beef Sandwich" with Caesar Salad on the side. Sorry, I'm putting air quotes because I don't have a very good memory of what happened a few days ago. Other than that, my order tasted so good especially with sauce that it came with. It was yummy in my tummy and I was satisfied with it. The employees working at the restaurant in my point of view were doing a good job even though they just opened recently. I'm really glad I gave La Madeleine a try and I would like to come back again in the future. It would be nice to treat my sister and my brother in-law and they would go nuts with the nice, delectable selection of desserts but I wouldn't get my hopes up just yet. All in all, I hope and pray that this restaurant will do fine and get better in the future as time goes on. I'll visit again, later on.

reviewText: I had to do a business trip to a certain merchant around this area, and decided to go to La Madeleine. I just moved here from Tennessee not too long ago, so I have never tried this place before. I decided to get a sort of chicken pot pie, and sat outside. The first bite was excellent, and then the second bite, I heard a large crunch sound. I pulled out a dime right out of my mouth like some magician. I was terrified on what happened. I did not want to make a big scene, so I nicely went over to one of the workers there, and just explained to them what happened so they can just be aware ... and just take more precaution so it does not happen to someone else. The worker apologized so much, and was saying sorry like no other. She had asked me if I wanted a replacement meal, and I kindly declined, as I did not want to have them make me another meal when they were already busy. As I was about to leave, the lady was so very kind to actually hand me a to go box with a fresh meal, and insisted that I'd take it. I thanked her for what she did, and left. This time, there was no dime in my food. Sadly, I do not think I will be going to La Madeleine, just because I feel like if I see their food, I'm seeing a dime with it too. But over all, that first bite was excellent.

reviewText: On the way home from work, we visited LA MADELINE FRENCH BAKERY & CAFE for dinner, and had an unimpressive culinary experience. The atmosphere is very nice - especially the big warm flaming fireplace on a cold winter evening - but the food was bland and tasteless. We ordered the French Onion Soup and Original Caesar Salad for appetizers, then the Salad Sampler and the Salmon with Kale & Butternut Squash. The French Onion Soup was tasty, but lacked enough cheese and tasty bread. The Salads were quite good - maybe the best part of our dinners. But my Salmon was overcooked, dry and tastless - like a re-heated frozen dinner. We've been to Paris and other cities in France dozens of times, and this was definitely NOT quality French cuisine! Maybe mediocre Parisian café fast-food. To add insult to injury, they only offer 3 selections of tasteless house wine: White, Red, and Rose. A French Restaurant? Yeah Right. There are several other bonifide French restaurants in Old Town and NorthEast. We are not wasting our money again. La Madeline's is NOT RECOMMENDED.

reviewText: 11/12/23: DISAPPOINTED on multiple counts.. It is my son's birthday today & our household has been sick with a flu/cold for a week - altho we are finally starting to recover we are still extremely congested & coughy so conscientiously chose "To Go" online order vs eating inside (which might've gotten employees & other customers sick). I arrived early, called & informed them that I was outside for whenever the food was ready to please bring it out - they said ok. Time elapses & it's now a few minutes before ready time (order said it would be ready 8:12pm) so I asked my sister who is not sick to go inside to check on the order - oddly, the food was all bagged & waiting on the counter for us (me wondering how long the food sat on the counter..). My sister brought the food to the car & I ensured everything was there & spotted the onion soup had no cheese nor croutons/toast so she went back in & she informed them - they said it's supposed to have them (we know, that's why we pointed out they were missing) & gave her a side baggie of those items. 15 minutes later we arrive home with the $90 meal including a whole Sacher Torte (my son's Birthday cake). At least the 4 diff soups were warm & delicious. The Quiche Lorraine was luke warm at best. The Crêpe la Madeleine was cold - yuck (me wondering again how long the food sat on the counter!?). I opened the Strawberry Spinach Bacon Salade & notice no dressing anywhere - I start eating but realize there's tons of bad soggy decaying spinach - gross! Not a happy camper & hope I don't get food sick 🤬 At least the Sacher Torte (we've ordered it most years for my son's birthday) was delicious altho a bit smudged.. altho much better than the year I picked it up & it had cracks all over it due to someone not making/storing it properly. Unfortunately it seems like the quality standards at La Madeleine is going downhill (their salads used to be top notch & hot foods served hot) - I have no doubt they would've fixed these things had I been eating onsite & raised them in person but alas I was sick at my home 15 minutes. By the time our meal ended around 9:15pm La Madeleine was already closed (they close at 9pm) - much too tired from my illness to deal with calling them & having the rectify the issues some how..

reviewText: Was passing through Albuquerque and looking for a place for a nice dinner. Saw this place, looked at the menu online, and decided to try it. Big mistake. reviewText: Two stars because the pastries are excellent. La Madeline absolutely ruined my Mother's Day morning. I'm a divorced mom so I don't get showered with gifts and I have to treat myself. I started planning my day the day before and planned to have a mimosa, eat a chocolate croissant, drink some good coffee and relax away my morning. I planned ahead and found that La Madeline has curbside pickup. I order pastries for me and the kids along with a mimosa for curbside pick up. The first thing I noticed was that there were two different telephone numbers on the confirmation email I received. I thought it was obvious that the number with the 201 area code was a typo but when I called the local store number, it sounded as if someone picked up and hung up. I had to get out of my car, defeating the purpose of curbside pickup and walk to to where about 20 delivery drivers were waiting to ask about my order. The lady wrote my name down and said she would check. I went back to my car and finally got through via phone. It was about 11:40 and my order was scheduled to be ready at 11:30. I was told they'd have my order out in a moment. I waited and waited. I spoke to someone next after 12 and was told they ran out of pastries and had to bake more muffins and croissants I reconfirmed where I was parked and the make, model and color of my vehicle. I waited and waited I next called to speak to someone around 1pm after I debated leaving but knew I wouldn't be able to find breakfast anywhere else at that time. Marie, the lady I had spoken to previously asked my name and where I was parked as if I hadn't spoken to her before. Ten minutes later I saw someone waking toward my car. My mimosa wasn't there so I asked for it and it was brought to me minutes later by another lady who looked at my children in the car and wished me a Happy Mother's Day. My morning Mother's Day plans were absolutely ruined as I had spent the morning parked in the La Madeline parking lot waiting for pastries. I had a terrible experience and all I wanted to do was cry. Marie, the lady who answers calla for curbside pickup never gave me a clear time frame for when my order would be ready and in the hour and a half it took for my order to arrive, I watched delivery drivers come and go and saw people drive up, go in and order and leave with their orders. Terrible experience! If my coworkers or the owner of our firm suggest LA Madeleine for weekly lunches or Friday breakfast orders ever again, my answer will be no.

reviewText: I was not impressed during my visit today. Walking in, the atmosphere is nice, if a bit sterile. A sign indicated where to go to dine in -- but it turns out that you don't do that. Rather, you stand at the entrance of the restaurant with other patrons and look at a menu. When you're ready, you tell someone holding a tablet what you want, and then you go to a cafeteria-style line and repeat what you just ordered to them. Then, you reach a register at the end, and you tell the cashier for a third time what your order was. There are several logistical questions I have about this process, but the foremost one is: why do things so inefficiently? Our food came quickly once we sat down, but it was nothing to write home about. Everything was both quite salty and bland, though I do think that the bread my sandwich came on was fantastic and soft. Still, a meal for two with a latte was just under $30, which is absurd for the quality of the food. As an aside, there is a little table where you can get bread slices, butter, and jam, which is a nice touch -- but the butter was in little plastic containers, and every tiny dollop of jam was in another plastic container, which is needlessly wasteful. Pros: Friendly staff, clean restaurant, decent selection, the desserts looked good. Cons: Ordering process built on disorder, mediocre salty food, high prices, lots of wasted plastic.

reviewText: Very inefficient order system which is frustrating to the customer and results in a lot of employees standing around doing nothing. In addition, all the employees seem to have been given different instructions as none of them could agree on anything (ie - get your desserts at the cashier but when you get to the cashier she tells you she doesn't do that - you have to go to the "to go" line to order desserts; order taker says you get your salad from the salad person, only to be told by the salad person that since it is a "side" it comes on your plate). Overall, as a customer, I found this whole process confusing and frustrating. The customer in front of me had to go back to the order taker half way through the process because where you order "french toast" is with the order taker, not the "hot grill plate" person. The food came out quickly after the 1/2 hour wait to order and get through the process. It was okay - not great but okay. The dessert was very good though. I think I will wait awhile before going back and will modify this review if things improve. For now, I recommend staying away as they work out the kinks. Advise to the management - reconsider the whole order taking process - maybe put in "ordering stations (multiple)" or consider having a few order takers.

reviewText: La Madeleine? We walked into a lifeless atmosphere, greeted by a host whose demeanor matched the room — dreary and unwelcoming. Trying to look past first impressions proved to be a mistake. The bakery area looked disheveled, with pastries that appeared stale and no inviting aroma to suggest anything fresh was being made. Service was nearly nonexistent. We had to grab our own menus and seat ourselves, surrounded by dirty, uncleared tables. Even after waiting, no one came to take our order, so we went up to the counter. When our food arrived, the tables around us were still filthy, and we received no utensils or guidance on where to find them. The food itself was no saving grace. My beef crepe stroganoff was bland, with meat that looked and tasted like processed canned beef. The entire dish turned my stomach, and I felt unwell even after returning home. La Madeleine in Gaithersburg is a disorganized, poorly managed, and unappetizing establishment. I’d sooner grab breakfast from a fast food drive-thru than set foot in here again.

reviewText: First of all, the hours state they are OPEN until 10. We arrived at 9:45 coming into town from a long trip looking to make a to go order. The doors were already locked. We went back for lunch today. There were several people working, 3 available to help through the salad line and it seemed no one wanted to. Finally the girl who did help looked like she hated life. My salad was made sloppy and my cup of soup bowl was dirty. Our glasses for our drinks were foggy and wet indicating they had been washed but they were turned upside down which could harbor bacteria if not aired out properly. Once I dried it with a napkin, there were water stains and smudges. as we ate and people left, tables were not bused or cleaned off. A man spilled his drink trying to clean off a table himself to eat at and still no one came to his aid or offered to replace his drink. We then went to the bakery counter to get dessert. There was one person working it although like I said earlier, there was someone standing at the register for an empty salad line and the girl who helped with soups went to the back. One man kept walking back and forth but did not offer to help the individual behind the counter. Because the bakery worker was alone he kept walking away from customers to get boxes for to go desserts as they were speaking. He also had to manage the register. The line was backing up almost out the door so we left. I personally have worked at a la Madeline and I've been to several in different cities. This had to be the most poorly maintained and run location I've ever visited. The customer service was below par and the functionality of workers and roles was non existent. Hopefully changes can be made to ensure a cleaner environment and enhanced overall experience.

reviewText: Bonjour! I typically don't write reviews that include the good and the challenging, BUT in this case and after some thought, I decided to do so. I am a long term patron of la Madeleine locations since high school. The Preston Rd. location in Dallas was actually my very first job (during the time when Patrick was still involved). And during this time of Covid and inability to travel internationally, the Lakeline location in Austin has given me a small "taste" of what I miss, enjoying a coffee and croissant in France. I have always found Melinda to be a wonderful asset to the location (and la Madeleine as a whole) which is why I choose that location vs. others in Austin. She's always been kind, professional, sincere and especially patient during what appeared to be the most challenging times... like yesterday. I am not certain what the end result was, but yesterday one of the cooks was heard arguing with Melinda over what seemed, "bacon". I don't know the prep/cooks , so I don't have a name (and wouldn't share in a public forum like this, anyway). I was surprised and disappointed, especially because Lakeline is always so pleasant to visit for enjoying a bite, a drink, listening to the cafe's music (when not busy) and/or getting some work done. Obviously, I understand that work places, especially those in hospitality and retail, come with a great deal of stress. I sincerely hope that yesterday's lack of professionalism and disrespect (in my opinion) isn't a sign of the future for this otherwise, lovely location. I hope this is read by the Corporate office and that perhaps some conflict management/communication can be done, if not already. And I hope that Melinda is supported as much as she supports her patrons (even the ones who choose to treat her poorly). Until next time, KG

reviewText: I have been very disappointed lately in the taste, quality, and quantity of my food at this location. Everything used to be very fresh and flavorful. For quite some time the croissant itself has been much smaller than it used to be. The French Dip was made with what looked like cheap beef lunchmeat and the cheese was unrecognizable. Plus, it had minced onions on it that gave it a terrible aftertaste. Drinks aren’t much better. This location has been out of rose wine for months now. The brand is fairly common, and not expensive, so there seems to be no reason why. The water from the soda machine has not been clear for some time now, today it was light pink. Apparently this is a common occurrence according to the employee who I pointed it out to. She seemed very unconcerned. Service is lackluster, and the employees are more interested in visiting with each other than serving customers. I used to think this was one of the better locations but not anymore. I won’t stop going to La Madeleine but I won’t be returning to this location.

reviewText: Don't place delivery orders at this La Madeleine's location in Sugar Land Town Center! reviewText: I went in for breakfast this morning expecting a good experience; I have been to the South location and they are great. I ordered the spinach quiche and potatoe galette out of the display case. The quiche was fine; the galette was cold, but no big problems. My friend ordered strawberry French toast, which has to be made fresh. When the French toast was brought to the table, it was two pieces of dry, unbuttered toast with a few sliced strawberries and a messy drizzle of sweet cream. It looked nothing like any French toast I've ever seen. My friend brought the dish back to the front to ask about it, and the employee at the front counter immediately started yelling at him, loud enough for the whole café to hear. It was pretty clear that he was not willing to refund, replace, or change the order. Another staff member (I'm assuming a manager) came to our table a few minutes later and offered to bring something else (she was much more polite), but honestly, by then we just wanted to finish the food and get out of there. I understand that restaurants have their own "spin" on a lot of dishes, but there is no version of French toast that involves bread that hasn't been soaked, and besides that, the employee's reaction was completely unprofessional and very off-putting. I'm definitely not returning to this location or recommending it to others; if you really want to visit a la Madeleine location, I'd say it's worth it to drive the extra 30 minutes down to Brodie Lane and Ernest Robles.

reviewText: La Madeleine is a good place, however being French, I wouldn't say they are a French Bakery and Café per se. It's good but not very authentic. I would advise to go there if you don't know French food and want to be initiated slowly. It's a very Americanized French food. So beside my disappointment in looking for authentic French food, it's good, not too expensive. The other little malus of that chain is that it is difficult to get something without bacon, but that "issue" is common to lot of places in Texas as far as I know. Advise: just check their menu before going there to be sure they have something you could enjoy. Be aware that's a first step to try French food, but a good one if you are worried to not like French food. On a side note, and because I can't leave a review without talking about the crew working at a place: the team is nice, friendly and you shouldn't worry about bad service (except once in a while, because they are humans that can have a bad day like everybody else ;) )

reviewText: Have been here 3 different times of day and am glad I did! First was for coffee and croissants. The sauce could have benefitted from a tad more cream(okay I am a nitpicker), but was definitely good enough to take leftovers home for lunch. The third time was for Sunday breakfast. Perfectly cooked eggs. I will try their croque Monsieur and pain perdu, on future visits. We will make this a regular stop. P.S. This is order at the desk, get delivered to table service. Pick up utensils at the drinks bar. There is a cozy gas fireplace. The ceilings are too high for an intimate dinner....It is somewhere between an upscale cafeteria(no disrespect meant) and full service restaurant/ coffeebar.
