reviewText: After visiting other La Madeleine locations, I wasn't ever overly impressed. Today I visited this location and was blown away. Not only by the tasty food, but by the amazing service. I walked in with my 4 year old and 2 year old. I came I to contact with 4 different employees and they were gracious, polite, and beyond helpful and just genuinely friendly (extremely hard traits to find in employees these days)! They were engaging with my kids and just all around warm! I unknowingly ordered a pesto pasta with cheese (my youngest can't have dairy) and tried to order one without cheese and willingly pay for it, because obviously it was my mistake. The chef insisted that he would make it again, without dairy, at no charge. I tried to give back the pasta with cheese bc we hadn't touched it, yet. He smiled and told me to feed someone else with and wished my a good day. I was blown away! La Madeleine can be on the pricey side when feeding 4 peop, but I will most definitely be back to this location!

reviewText: I've tried to enjoy this restaurant on multiple occasions. At first, I gave them the benefit of doubt due to them recently opening the Louisiana location. Now that it's been almost a year and the quality of service had only gotten worse and more inconsistent. Pros: The recipes offered are tasty. It's also nice to see a company calling themselves a bakery that actually makes loaves of bread. Good salads are hard to find in Albuquerque. They offer a couple interesting selections. Cons: Inconsistent. Occasionally I'm greeted with a smile right away, most of the time I wait without acknowledgement while several people stand with their backs to me even when there is no line. The quantity of food is different every time. Out of the last ten visits, I was satisfied with the serving size four of them. Paying 12+ dollars a salad is fine but sometimes it's only about one cup of greens. When I order to go, the container it's served in is always different even though I ordered the same exact meal. Once, when I got home, there was a big mess in the bag. Pasta sauce leaked everywhere. After I ate most of it, I noticed a hole was cut out of the bottom! The quality is usually good, but several times I had to throw away half the salad due to rot and what looks like freezer burn. I've also had my delicate pastries served on its side several times. Now I sit feeling like I've eaten week old fried carnival food when I should feel great and refreshed from my Caesar salad. These problems should have been remedied by now. I have given them a dozen or so chances and it's time for me to realize the hype of a 'French' bakery with prices high enough to compete in San Francisco is not what it claims.

reviewText: The food is great and the prices are better than other fast-casual chains. They face one major flaw...service. You order your food at a counter with a restaurant associate and an IPad but there isn't a large menu posted anywhere. So, people are looking through a paper menu with a line 10 people deep. Once you get through that line, you get the joy of waiting in another line to pay. The associates then bring your food to your table. The last three times I've been there, it's taken 20-30 minutes for my food to arrive at the table. Even though the wait has been long, the food doesn't disappoint for a "fast-casual" chain. The portions are a perfect size and the food always tastes great. The desserts are delicious if you want something to treat yourself!

name: la Madeleine
fullAddress: 8134 Agora Pkwy #100, Selma, TX 78154, United States
reviewText: I am beyond disappointed with our experience at La Madeleine at The Forum. What we encountered was not just poor service, it was unacceptable and embarrassing for a brand that presents itself as a French-inspired-bakery-café with an upscale, boutique image. The restaurant was clearly and dangerously understaffed. The line to order moved at a crawl because the hostess was forced to juggle multiple roles. Once we finally placed our order, the wait for food was excessive, and when it arrived, the quality was inexcusable. One member of our family, someone who never complains, immediately notified the waiter that his two scrambled eggs were cold. In a shocking and unprofessional response, the waiter put his finger into the eggs to confirm they were cold and then removed the plate. That moment alone demonstrated a complete lack of food-handling standards and training. It also left us questioning whether the food was properly remade or simply reheated and returned. My daughter’s bacon was raw and completely inedible. The French toast was burned on the side that was intentionally not visible, which felt deceptive. My own French toast was served lukewarm, not hot. When customers order freshly prepared food, they reasonably expect it to be served at the proper temperature. This is a basic standard, not a luxury. The operational failures did not stop there. The restaurant did not have spoons available, and when my daughter asked at the counter, she was told they were all in the dishwasher. The same excuse was given when we requested knives. The raw sugar container had only two packets left, and there was no staff member available to replenish it or assist us. To make matters worse, the hallway leading to the restrooms had several trash cans lined up with towels underneath, actively catching water from a roof leak. This was alarming from both a cleanliness and safety standpoint and should never be visible to customers. Overall, this experience was worse than dining at a budget breakfast chain. For La Madeleine to deliver a dining experience that falls below the standards of IHOP is frankly astonishing. Whether this location is cutting costs by refusing to staff properly, suffering from constant employee turnover, or experiencing severe management failure, the result is the same: customers are paying for a brand promise that is not being delivered. People go out to eat expecting quality food, basic cleanliness, and competent service. This location failed on every level. Until serious operational and management issues are addressed, I would strongly caution others against dining here.

reviewText: Oh...I don't know. Perhaps only giving it 3 stars is a bit harsh, but there are some details being missed here which I think are worth reviewing. First, the food. That said, I get the sense that they use their microwave extensively for re-heating...and their quiche usually tastes like it has been sitting under heat lamps for an extensive amount of time. This isn't make or break, but it's a detail that might be something to look at if I were management. It shouldn't take that much to keep food fresh and hot without the use of microwaves or long heat lamp durations. The salads are great. Deserts are good. reviewText: Terrible! Terrible! I drove 20 miles very excited to visit La Madeline as it is one of my favorites in Texas. I talked my daughter into driving 20 miles as well and assured her it was worth it. How embarrassing for this company. My first contact was at the register where it says line starts here and the waitress or a bus person said this isn’t open go down to the other register with no smile no apology. I noticed there was no food along the service area in the glass window at all, which is strange because there is always delicious looking food to view.OK maybe she was having an off day. I enthusiastically approached the second register and when I explained where we came from and how excited we were to be there, she asked “why would you do that? There is one in Santan Valley”. I explained to her I was from the opposite direction that is why I chose her restaurant. She seemed baffled but now I know why. I’ll shorten the story up. They were out of half-and-half so I asked for heavy cream and the manager just looked at the waitress and asked three times why. I chimed in and said because “you’re out of half-and-half”, so he gave me heavy cream in a coffee mug and just said “here” with no smile no apology. My quiche came five minutes after my daughters plate. The crust was hard as a rock. My potato galette was definitely one to two days old and cold on the plate. I flagged down the waitress and asked for the side of béarnaise sauce that I ordered and she said what is béarnaise sauce? I advised her it’s a French restaurant and béarnaise sauce is common and she didn’t know what I was talking about. I pointed to someone else’s béarnaise sauce and she just walked away and came back with a cup of Béarnaise sauce that was cold. I ordered crisp bacon and clearly they microwaved it and burned it. I had to apologize to my daughter for making her drive 20 miles for the worse breakfast I’ve had all year. This store needs quality control from corporate in the worst way. Please get this store in shape so you can be represented correctly. The French coffee was great and the fireplace was nice and that’s the only positive thing I can say for my visit.

reviewText: La Madeleine has been an established cafe for over a decade within Austin. launching with high appraisal it seemed clear this cafe had a lot of potential for a prosperous and delicious legacy. sadly, I am not here to give praise to this establishment today; walking in on this Monday afternoon I was excited to have a wonderful French inspired brunch experience. it came to a shock to me that a place with 4 stars overall would be so empty. Stained floors, clear signs of water damage, and an empty restaurant set the tone for what I was getting into quickly. I ordered the French breakfast, a $12 meal with eggs, sausage, croissant, and a potato galette. Looking at my late it was clear not a single one of these items listed were made from scratch. the flavorless eggs were clearly powdered eggs, the bland paper-thin sausage patty reheated from a frozen bag, and the croissant was the equivalent of one you would have at Sams club. I was given complementary "bread" that had the distinct taste of plastic. So far this has been one of the worst meals I have had, you are truly better off eating dinning somewhere else. overall, it was clear La Madeleine is well past its golden years and is yet another failing cafe to be closed in a few years if no changes are made.

reviewText: Made an order for pick up online a couple of weeks ago. I followed the steps online to order and after paying I got a confirmation email and pick up time. reviewText: I used to work at la Madeline's (Sundance Square) many years ago. I had nothing but the fondest memories of those times. Saute and Prep, I learned a lot about cooking and restaurants. The pastries and bread items were incredible and nicely portioned. I still love the place, but I think the portions on the pastries have gotten significantly smaller. Food is a bit more expensive (sign of the times) The new fruit tart seems smaller for the same price. The French coffee is amazing still, almond croissants are fire! Croissants are still soft and buttery. The parking situation at this store is fugly, tiny lot (shared with Starbucks and it's drive through) in a VERY busy shopping center near Costco. I still love coming here, just not as often as I used to. I hit that Camp Bowie location all the time when I lived over there. I think you would enjoy: Breakfast - French Country Breakfast, strawberries Romanoff, Quiche Lorraine, or potato galette. Lunch - Chicken Friand w/mushroom sauce, tomato basil soup, potato soup, French onion soup, croque monsior, chicken Parisian sandwich, or French dip. Dinner - chicken la Madeline or Pesto Pasta.

reviewText: I’ve been here many times and never leave dissatisfied. This location has been here for at least 15+ years and is still popular in NW Austin. reviewText: It was ok, nothing bad at all. My partner and I both loved the atmosphere and the decor, and the staff wasn't mean or anything like that. The food was fine, though we did have some nitpicks. My crepe was very mushy, and the croissant was served cold which is strange as normally they seem to be warmed at least by default in other places. My partner thought that his Croque Monsieur (Forgive me if I misspelled that) was just ok, and expected it to be creamier. I did love the coffee, and my hard boiled eggs were done very well. The plating and presentation was nice as well. Other than that we really weren't too impressed by the food and aren't too inclined to go back soon. We also did not know that we had to go right up to order, rather than wait to be seated, which confused us initially as there was no indication of what to do. Overall, my first impression is that it's a restaurant with lovely atmosphere and average food. It's not a bad place to go at all, but probably could make more improvements and little changes to be even better than it is currently.

reviewText: When it comes to French cafes in Houston, you can't go wrong with Le Madeleine. Been coming to this location for over five years now. Although it's pretty much self service ordering at the buffet line, the waitstaff is always happy to help out, clearing plates and getting condiments. Highly recommend for singles, couples, families, and groups.

reviewText: My husband went to the Chandler La Madeleine for breakfast this morning. The young man who took our order was surly. He never smiled. He seemed as if he really did not want to be there. I asked for "crisp bacon" with my order. I asked him, "can your cook do crisp bacon?". He answered "Yes." When I got my order, the bacon was limp and fatty. The woman who brought us our food was nice and helpful. I asked her to cook my bacon some more, to make it crisp, and she said she would get me a new order of bacon. When I got the new bacon, it was crisp because it was black (burned). Apparently no one in the kitchen this morning knew how to cook bacon. While our meal in general tasted good, my husband's plate gave the impression of being slapped together with no care taken about how it looked. I had a latte with my meal and my husband had an espresso. Both coffees were great. To sum up, the food tasted good, but the surly youth's attitude, the bacon issue and the lack of attention given to presentation caused us to conclude that eating breakfast there just wasn't worth what it cost. I should add that I have eaten lunch multiple times at the La Madeleine in downtown Phoenix, and it was great every time, in every respect. Perhaps the problem is just with the Chandler branch, and some (but not all) members of the breakfast-shift crew.

reviewText: A few weeks ago I went to get some food at this place around 8pm, the attendants were chatting near the dinne-in register, ignoring the customers coming in. reviewText: Rather than making sure the order was correct, the person taking orders seemed more worried about making sure everyone in our party of 6 understood that she would let us know if we needed a tray after 3 of us already had trays with glasses on them. She also mentioned that we could combine our glasses and soups so we didn't all need a tray! We were down to 3 trays already! More time spent trying to reduce tray usage! Still plenty of trays available. All soups were barely warm enough to melt the cheese. My Croque Monsieur was soggy from too much uncooked cheese on the outside rather than the toasted cheese it should have had. Same thing on my daughter-in-law's Croque Madame. All and all a very sad experience for our granddaughters 16th birthday lunch...it used to be her favorite place for our special outings. Silverware are off to the side and you can help yourself to their complimentary bread. I remember coming here a while ago with a party in one of their private room. reviewText:
As you walk in, your eyes are greeted with beautiful walnut stained wood arches complete with a gas fire, which will make you want to grab a front row seat. The overall bistro set up is nice unless it’s your first time.

I am usually in autopilot if I haven’t had my morning cup of coffee, so my focus isn’t all there. I appreciate the patience of the employees, it means a lot. What I like about this sublime bistro, is its warm french atmosphere.

The ONLY two things that I think I would improve on is just warming up the pastries but don’t burn them. Also customer service could be brought up a little bit but the effort put forth in trying to be nice is noteworthy.

Overall, this place so cute and I love it. It would be nice if we had one of these in Washington State!

reviewText: When it's time to have brunch with my friends or if my boyfriend and I want to get a little fancy without breaking the bank, this is the best place to go. reviewText: It's not often that I am driven to post a comment or review for an eating establishment. Either its for exceptional service or disappointing, in this case its the latter. Today I ordered lunch online and arrived 10 minutes after the scheduled pickup time. I followed the instructions for curb pickup, by dialing the provided number when I arrived and the designated location and keyed in the number to be asked for my identifying vehicle, etc. The phone rang without being picked up for 30 minutes. Irritated that I had to then find a non curbside pickup location, I re-parked my car and went inside to find my order. At the indoor register where two employees and maybe a half-dozen seated customers, spread the safety distance within the restaurant area. I eyed my order on the counter and waited for the employee nearest me to acknowledge my presence. When she did I asked was there a problem with the phone service, due to the fact that no one picked up the curbside line? She said to her knowledge it was working. I then told her that I had been waiting thirty minutes in the pickup zone, with no one answering the line. I even showed her the number, when questioned about whether I dialed correctly! Well, the number was from the email reply, I showed her what it was and she then believed me. I informed her my cold food order had at that time been sitting at room temperature for nearly and hour, judging from the time stamp on the bag receipt, and she offered to have it remade, and have the manager come out to address my situation. Five minutes after this brief discussion, the manager (or what appeared to be the manager) walks out behind the counter and towards the end I was located, over to the pickup shelf, retrieves an order for a deliver service, and goes out the door, without evening stopping to acknowledge my presence. WOW! Talk about discourteous service. The counter clerk glanced at me quickly, before disappearing. I don't think I will be patronizing this location again, and please be warned, don't attempt to use curbside pickup here, unless you want to be totally ignored.

reviewText: I have been enjoying coffee and eating while finishing work at La Madeline for nearly a decade now as I get closer to wrapping up my schooling in its entirety. I have also servered tables for extra income nearly every semester. I know the business well. Food cannot always come out perfect (temperature, timing, and even sometimes taste). However, customer service is the equivalent of that problem a professor puts on an exam to ensure you get some points. As I slide my tray to the cash register there is a gentleman wearing a red shirt with a full beard at the register. He never makes eye contact, he fumbles with some money, and after a long while waiting to pay he looks to an employee and request they pay me out. Never said a word to me. Of course, she comes over and struggles because the cash drawer is under him, which was confirmed when he said, "You can only log in with sliding the card if the drawer is under you," then slides his card. I can only assume he is management which is why it was so disappointing. Get the points where they are handed to you this way there is room for some error coming from true mistakes. This note is mostly for La Madeline to ensure continued growth and happy guest.

reviewText: Upon entering this place was a little confusing regarding the set up. It was hard to tell how it worked, where to order, and what to do since it was our first time. There was a line and two people behind the counter tending to the people getting pastries. Then someone else came out on the other end of the counter and said we ordered there. Once we figured it all out though it was really good. We had soup and pastries and I had a coffee. The coffee was excellent. One coffee gave me a lot of grounds but as soon as I told an employee it was removed and a fresh one was brewed and brought out. The coffee was very, very tasty. They also have some good flavored teas. They free bread was a nice touch too and they have excellent preserves to go with it. The creme brulee was fantastic too! I will go back for sure. I just suggest having a little more staff or signs so people are aware of what is going on and may not get frustrated and leave. Also, the French lessons in the bathroom are a nice touch.

reviewText: Delicious assortment of meals to choose from. Friendly and helpful staff. Beverage & bread stations are in the dining area so you can serve yourself. The cafe ambience is nice, with a rustic French setting. Get their mobile app and receive offers/rewards. reviewText: On day 2 of their official opening, La Madeleine has some of the usual issues any new business would have. Service hiccups and incorrect orders, I am able to sympathize with and not judge too harshly. What really helped me overlook past these problems was the creamy wild mushroom sauce and coconut cream cake! After being kindly greeted in french, we placed our order, paid and took the food pager with us to the table of our choice. Complimentary slices of their sourdough and whole wheat bread were offered with mini cups of jam and butter to accompany you while you wait for your food. I picked "Chicken La Madeleine," one of their signature dishes . This entree arrived composted of a balsamic marinated chicken breast with a delicious wild mushroom cream sauce, nicely done broccoli and rice provincal that was a tad on the soggy side. "Pasta La Madeleine's" shrimp missed the boat, for the sauce was thin, runny and flat on the taste buds. Showing what they do best, La Madeleine shined at dessert time! The coconut cream cake was superb! I couldn't stop eating this wonderfully moist, layer cake that came stacked with flavor and endless sweetened, shredded coconut! I did appreciate the fireplaces, french accented decor and clean layout of this cafe. It makes for an inviting environment. In fact, I think I will be inviting myself back really soon........

reviewText: My girlfriend and I came here yesterday, we ordered a soup, a sandwich, an iced latte, a pre-packaged cookie and a croissant. The tomato basil soup was quite literally the worst tomato soup I have ever tasted. It tasted old and microwaved, and was sour beyond belief. How do you make a tomato basil soup so sour? We had ordered a baguette on the side, they forgot it. My girlfriend and I both agreed their croissant was noticeably lower quality than the one we bought at Starbuck's earlier in the week. (Pitiful...) The sandwich I bought was a Large, it was called "Chicken Riviera". It was okay, but the bread was very hard almost to the point it hurt my mouth. It was also put together veryy sloppily, (avocado drenching the top-side of the sandwich bread) and they didn't even cut the large sandwich in half! What kind of bistro doesn't cut your large sandwich in half for you? It was put together so sloppily, I had to cut it in half myself before I could even attempt to eat it! The pre-packaged cookie was nice, but they don't make those in store. My iced latte was delicious, I will say. However, virtually everything else about the visit was extremely disappointing. We decided to give La Madeleine another try because I was tired of how often I find myself at Starbuck's for similar products. After this last time, I will never make that mistake again and I urge you to save your money as well, and probably more importantly; your time. The first time my girlfriend and I ate here a couple of months ago, we ordered two coffees and two pastries and it took 45 minutes for them to arrive at our table. Their laughable service is a running joke around Cedar Park honestly, a lot of people have heard about how miserably slow and unattentive they are. Of course we should show some sympathy for these restaurants who lost a lot of staff during Covid, but at the same time if a business simply does not possess the means to deliver to their customers the quality that they advertise, they should close down. La Madeleine may not care about customer satisfaction quite as much as they claim to.

reviewText: As simulations go of regional cuisine, La Madeline ain't half bad, although they certainly get some stuff much better than others. OMG, I love the soups, especially the Tomato Basil, which they're well aware of the popularity of, as they sell it to-go by the door. The deserts from the pasty bar are all quite delectable as well. It's the meals proper that have a variable quality, or, at least, don't feel very French farm house. I've never had anything I outright didn't like, but certainly have felt inspired to go try something a bit more regionally accurate for my next French craving after a so-so meal. But really, I'm being nitpicky for a place that does so much more good than bad, and quite a bit really great. This new location does away with the cafe trays and just has the staff bring everything to your table, which I appreciate. Certainly lots of friendly and perhaps even a bit over-attentive servers and a good eatin' spot right near the Lakeline Alamo for your pre-movie repast.

reviewText: I am a huge La Medeleine fan, but this particular location needs some serious help. We walked in and a younger lady was in front of asking for an application to work at the restaurant, the cashier had no idea where the applications were so she went and got the manager who also had no idea. While waiting 10 minutes for them to find the application the cashier could have had her step aside while she tended to us (and 3-4 other people in line behind us), but everyone had to wait for the manager to walk around (with a very slow pace) trying to find the correct paperwork. We finally got a chance to order and the cashier was just very awkward and slow in asking us what we wanted (she might have been new though so not a big deal). I specifically asked for the dressing of my salad to be mixed with the lettuce (to-go order which they usually give you dressing on the side). I checked my receipt as soon as I paid which said "Dressing on salad". We then waited around 15-20 minutes before I saw the same manager begin making our salads. It seemed like they were extremely understaffed for a Sunday afternoon. I can understand if someone called out sick or quit that day but the manager was working with absolutely zero urgency. The manager made the salad and put no dressing on which I asked her as soon as she bagged it to make it again and she looked at me rudely. She said I didn't ask for dressing to be mixed, and I said check the receipt and she looked and just put her head down and started making a new one. She then begin to make my wife's salad which has bacon on it. She bagged it up and I checked and noticed there wasn't any bacon, she took another 2-3 minutes to go find where the bacon was and returned with it in a container. As I was leaving out the door I overheard another patron say "The soda machine isn't working" Maybe it was just a bad day for this location, but having worked in retail you have to put up with it and show some urgency. If I saw her running around and going as fast as I thought she could, I would have been a little more patient and not written this review. Her lack of a good attitude and carelessness isn't acceptable and I will not be back to this location.

reviewText: The food La Madeleine offers is absolutely delicious. On quality of food alone I would rate La Madeleine as one of the top chains in San Antonio if not the United states far outstripping comparators (e.g. Panera). It may surprise you then that I rank - at least this location - so low. Please understand it takes a lot to earn such a low rating from me - not just a single bad experience but evidence of serious issues related to cleanliness, health, safety, or service. My negative experience started on Mother's day last year. I waited for two hours to receive my order and never got it. I called the phone number at curbside pickup pproximately every five minutes and got through maybe one time in ten. I went in multiple times (masked, socially distant, the whole nine yards) and each time was told another few minutes. After two hours, and missing the brunch I was supposed to host for my wife in the first place, I left. I was never reimbursed. Even after this infuriating experience, I gave them another shot. There were some mitigating circumstances, after all: many had the same idea as me for mother's day during the pandemic and their online ordering had obviously been overwhelmed. It was also early on in the pandemic and so I recognized that as much as it was frustrating, all businesses were struggling to adapt to the new way of doing business. So this morning, I gave them another try. I figure the morning of the superbowl would be an off day and not terribly busy. I pull up to curbside, call the number, and again no response. I wait a few minutes, call again; no response. I mask up and go inside. When i explain the situation, i get little sympathy. But here was the kicker: the man working the register, turns around, puts his gloved hand into his trousers from behind - not sure if he had an itch, was readjusting himself, or what - and then without changing gloves proceeds to transfer the fresh tray of croissants onto a dish. I don't care how good the food is, that is unsanitary and frankly disgusts me. Too many strikes. I'll never go back.

reviewText: If I could give this place 0 stars, I would. Here was my first and last experience at this location: The location closes at 10, and I live less than 1.5 mi from where it is. I placed an order and finalized it online at 8:20pm, and it stated that it would be ready at 8:40pm. Great. I ordered the Roasted Salmon with Dill Sauce, which was described to come with rice provençal, and "fresh roasted" asparagus. I added a side of broccoli and a cup of the bean soup and was set to go. Wonderful. I left my home a short while later and and arrived at 8:38pm. The lady at the register brought up my order and asked about the side of broccoli, saying that it came up as a replacement side for the asparagus. I told her that I wanted it in addition to the asparagus, and she okayed that and told my total. A young gentleman who was getting my other together asked me if I wanted rice with it since he asserted that I got broccoli instead, and I answered yeah, mentioning that I was under the impression that it came with the dish, and that I ordered a side of broccoli. He mentioned the extra charge on the register screen, of which I could not see myself, and said that he'd get the rice together for me, that they'd have to heat it up. I said alright, thanked him, and waited patiently after paying my $17, thinking it wouldn't be that long of a wait. Well, he came back and said that they were out of dill sauce... at this point, I'm a little annoyed, mind you, I'm a fairly patient person, but I couldn't help but consider how ridiculous this situation is becoming. I asked what other sauces they have, and he said there was a pesto sauce.. that again, he'd have to heat up. I didn't want a dry filet of salmon, so I said ok, having paid and everything, and sat down to wait even longer. A little after 9, my food comes, and I head out the door. Before getting in my car to go home, I checked my bag only to find that---yep, you guessed it, my asparagus was missing. I go back in and wait for another 10 min for them to get it, or rather, I find out later, microwave zap it along with the rest of my god-awful food--after sorting through the confusion that they were under the impression that I subbed it out for broccoli (which was 100% overcooked with ZERO seasoning). The salmon was overcooked and tough, warmed with a microwave, and the asparagus which was BROWN was wrapped in a foil pack with a little "Sat" sticker on it, referencing two days prior (today is Monday!!) Fresh vegetables my ass! On top of that, it carried a rancid odor that spoke to how old it really was. Long story short: BAD communication, SLOW service, HORRIFICALLY AWFUL food. I don't know how this place got 4 stars, but this will absolutely be the last time I go here, or at least to this location. Should've gone to Chick-fil-A for dinner instead. Ugh.

reviewText: Something has happened at LaMadeleine, over past year or so. There are several different locations where I have eaten for many years. (Of course, I am aware of change in prices of eggs) Today, I ate at Preston / Forest location & ordered French toast eggs & bacon. I was sitting outside because it was still lovely before noon.. When my food was delivered, bacon looked very greasy, eggs were not scorched this time.Thank goodness. French toast was cold. I went back in and told cashier. She told me I had to bring it back in.So I grabbed it to go box to put my eggs and bacon in. Then I dutifully brought plate back in. I waited 10 minutes or more, was eating other 2 food items, however , they were also not hot. I went back in and asked to speak with manager. She brought me a card for a free meal. I said "thank you, but I want my french toast" She told me they were remaking it. I did tell her, at that time, that rest of my breakfast was not hot either. However I ate it. In a few more minutes, she brought me a new plate of all food ordered. Guess what? Still not hot. I related this to her and said , I was taking eggs and bacon home, was not going to waste it!! I would reheat them there... I already had my go box. Probably more than an hour later, after I had run another errand in Center, dirty dishes were still on table outside as well as to other tables where patrons had been. Regards, Barbara

reviewText: This review is solely based on my experience on today. Suggested by my wife we went to dine. So to make a long story short....upon paying for our meal I was handed a dirty glass. Water spots I can handle but stuck on food residue I won't do. I gave the glass back and requested to use a togo cup instead. Fixed my water, wanted to add lemon, however the lemon container had not been replenished. The few in there looked as though they were in there from the day before. Also no straws available, they didn't put any more out until we were leaving. Taking our seat I sipped my water and it had a funny taste as if the drink/ice machine hadn't been cleaned in a while. I order the potato cake which I got in the line, and the provolone chicken rice bowl that I had to wait to be prepared and brought to me. My wife had to replace her utensil because the first one was still dirty with food particles. As I waited for my food I had eaten my potato cake but my additional dish had not come out. I noticed several customers after us receive their orders but I hadn't yet received mine. We had to check the receipt just to make sure they added the dish on our order. Well I sat and watched my wife eat her food alone. We did not have the pleasure of enjoying our meals together. Finally when we where getting ready to go, I'm guessing she was the manager, noticed we still had our letter tag on our table so she went to the back to check on what we were waiting on. We went to the counter to ask about the dish and finally it came out which I had to tell them I'll just get it to go. So they put it in a togo container handed it to me without a bag, without any utensils, and without an apology for the wait and inconvenience of having to take my meal to go because someone dropped the ball. It was not busy at all, numerous employees, but much disorganization. Needless to say this was my first experience visiting La Madeleine and will be my last time visiting La Madeleine. Additionally the food is subpar based on other restaurants in the area. Coconut cream cake taste store bought or brought in from off site not homemade. Customer service non existent beyond ordering and paying for your meal. Dishes not cleaned very well. No hello's or thank you's for coming. I hope others do not have the same experience I just had because this left a sour taste in my mouth.

reviewText: Was in La Madeleine for breakfast. I found the manager, Lester, to be apathetic and discourteous. My husband and I waited to place our order as Lester chatted with a worker. He did not ask us to excuse him while he handled whatvever non-emergency issue that was at hand nor did he acknowledge our presence. When I mentioned it to him, he gave me a blank stare. I suggested that he should have acknowledged that we were standing there. He said flatly "I spoke to you when you came in". I don't know if he did or didn't. I don't think he did. Whether he did or not, it had no relevance to our waiting for his little chat to end. He said nothing but just stood there waiting for us to place our order. We did. I ordered the potato galette and an order of bacon. I was told that the galette would take 10 minutes. I was okay with that. After several minutes, my husband received his order and I received 3 bacon slices. I suppose I could have stated I wanted to receive the potato galette and bacon at the same time. I did not realize that it was necessary to state the obvious. I returned the bacon order to the counter. A young woman at the counter told me the galette would be ready in few minutes. I told her that was fine but my bacon would be cold by then. I asked that the galette be served with bacon. She seemed personally offended. She took the plate and walked away without a word to me. Based on the prior poor customer-oriented response from the manager, her atttitude was not surprising. The galette and bacon was brought to me by the manager, Lester. Not a word was said about the delay, the inconvenience, nor the fact that my husband and I had come to have breakfast together, but were served several minutes apart. The food was fair, a little salty. The service is below par. We chose La Madeleines because is near our home in Champion Forest. Next time we will opt to go to our favorite breakfast spot, Le Peep's. It's worth the extra time and travel to the Westchase area for good food and much better service.

reviewText: I've been an avid La Madeline customer since the 1990s. When I first discovered La Madeline, I lived in Irving; however, Arlington's closest location, and I gladly drove for my favorite items. So, one can imagine my excitement when I learned that this location would open just minutes from my office. The excitement was short-lived; this new concept is nothing short of a fast-food chain that serves pre-packaged meals, a limited menu, and inflated prices. My lunch was served to me in a plastic sack (not even branded), no silverware, and stickers on my salad as if I had purchased it from 7-11. This review is not a reflection of the employees at this location but the corporation. Over the years, I've seen subtle changes to the brand but have accepted it, but this change has surpassed the limitations I'm willing to accept. Sadly, I won't return to this location.

If restaurants want people to keep coming back, they need to treat accuracy and service as a priority, not an afterthought.

reviewText: Why a commodity surcharge for every purchase? Even on a single beverage La Madeleine's charges a .50 surcharge. This is ridiculous and has changed my desire to go to any LaMadeleine's now. There is another place near me that has the same mango tea for the same price and a larger cup with no surcharge. So where do you think I'll go? This location has gotten progressively worse. While I think the manager is great and always tries to make things right I think it is corporate that he has to follow and corporate is out of touch. With the new to-go counter, it has smaller portions for higher prices and they still charge the commodity fee. I refuse to pay for lower quality, higher prices, and smaller portions. Most customers will not either. La Madeleine's please listen to your customers and make some changes. Drop the surcharge and the tip function. LaMadeleine's is not a restaurant with wait staff. Handing me a cup to fill myself or handing me a bag from a to go counter is not serving and not deserving of a tip. Just pay your people more, drop the surcharge and the tip function and you'll see more customers coming back.
